title: SURE: Robust, Explainable, and Fair Classification without Sensitive Attributes

problem.claim: A classifier that is accurate on average may underperform for sensitive subsets, while a fair classifier should perform well for all sensitive subsets.

gap.claim: Sensitive subsets are often not known in advance, motivating performance across subsets likely to be sensitive.

contributions.claim: An iterative algorithm called SURE identifies statistically significant high-risk zones in feature space and adjusts loss weights for points in those zones to build a fair classifier.
SURE emphasizes statistical significance to make the method robust to noise.
SURE's high-risk zones are interpretable, and each method step is explainable through significance tests.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that SURE is fast and parameter-free.
Experiments on simulated and real-world datasets report that SURE is competitive with the state of the art.

narrative_sequence.summary: Average classifier accuracy can conceal underperformance for sensitive subsets.
Fair classification should perform well across sensitive or potentially sensitive subsets, even when those subsets are unknown beforehand.
SURE iteratively detects statistically significant high-risk feature-space zones and changes loss weights for their points.
The method is described as robust to noise, interpretable, explainable, fast, and parameter-free.
Experiments on simulated and real-world datasets report competitiveness with the state of the art.

source_observation.claim: When sensitive subsets are unknown, the method searches for statistically significant high-risk zones in feature space.

interpretation.claim: Fairness interventions can target empirically identified risk regions instead of requiring sensitive-group labels in advance.

application.claim: Use statistically significant subgroup-risk discovery to guide adaptive loss weighting in settings where sensitive attributes are unavailable.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish how well the approach works when sensitive risk is weakly represented or not statistically detectable.

source_observation.claim: The method explains each step through significance tests and reports robustness to noise.

interpretation.claim: Statistical testing can provide a shared mechanism for both robustness and explanations.

application.claim: Prefer auditable statistical decision rules when a classifier must expose why fairness-related adjustments were made.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the noise conditions, significance thresholds, or explanation quality criteria.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, evaluation metrics, or numerical results.
The abstract does not define the statistical tests, risk thresholds, or loss-weighting procedure.
The abstract does not establish independent verification of the reported competitiveness, speed, or parameter-free behavior.
